why: X4.1: a macro import leaves no statement; its name has no place
X4.1: an import from bun:bundle leaves no statement
X4.3: the body of an interface is not built; every identifier token in it is a read, its own name too
X4.3: the type of an alias is not built; its own name in it is a read
X4.3: a property name in an unbuilt type is a read of the variable of that name
code: const foo = 1; export type F = (x: number) => { foo: string };

why: X4.3: a parameter name in an unbuilt signature is a read of the outer variable of that name
code: const foo = 1; export interface I { m(foo: string): void }

why: X4.3: `typeof x` in an unbuilt type is a plain read: no 'only used as a type'
code: const foo = 1; export interface I { m(x: string): typeof foo }

why: X4.3: a type parameter declared inside an unbuilt type has no variable

why: the names in the parameters of a signature are read from the tokens: a type keyword that is a variable name marks that variable
code: const string = 1; export declare function f(x: string): void;

why: only when the whole signature is scanned and not its parameter list alone
code: const foo = 1; export declare function f(x: number): typeof foo;

why: only when the type visitor visits the annotation of a catch binding; typescript-eslint does not
code: import { T } from 'x'; try {} catch (e: T) { e; }

why: an empty statement after the return leaves no statement: the block has one statement for bun, two for typescript-eslint
